We have a target molecule: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We need retrosynthesis up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to propose route using templates.

We have one template (38653) that seems to convert a cyclic acetal? The template: [C:1]/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[C:4]>>[C:1]-[C@@H;D3;+0:2]1-O-[C@H;D3;+0:3]-1-[C:4]

So forward reaction: a cyclic acetal (dioxolane?) formed from a carbonyl and a diol? Actually reverse: retro step breaks a cyclic acetal to give an alkene and a carbonyl? The template applied to target gave two possible precursors (both not buyable). They are:

1) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

2) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C[C@@H]2O[C@H]2/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

These are similar but differ in position of double bond.

We need to break down further.

The target has a cyclic acetal (maybe a 1,3-dioxolane fused?) Actually structure: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Looks like a bicyclic? Might be a protected diol with a side chain unsaturated acid.

We can consider disconnection: The cyclic acetal could be formed from a diol and an aldehyde/ketone. The template suggests opening to give an alkene and a carbonyl? Wait the retro template: [C:1]/[CH]=[CH]/[C:4] -> cyclic acetal. So forward: cyclic acetal -> alkene + carbonyl? Actually the retro direction is the arrow: left side is product (alkene) and right side is reactant (cyclic acetal). So applying retro to target gave precursors that are alkenes with a side chain? The precursors are still cyclic? They have O[C@@H]... still cyclic? They have O[C@@H]... O[C@H]1... So still cyclic? Actually they have O[C@@H]... O[C@H]1... So they are still cyclic but maybe a different arrangement.

Maybe we need other templates.

Let's search for templates that break ether (since we have ether). Use get_available_functional_groups to see correct name: "ether oxygens". So we can break ether.

Search for templates breaking ether oxygens.
